models_evaluated: CTransPath encoder with attention-based multiple instance classifier (semi-automated confidence-threshold pipeline)

links.outcome: Lineage accuracy: fully automated vs routing low-confidence cases to IHC/pathologist review
links.effect: Fully automated model had a 16.1% accuracy decrease in the prospective cohort (p<0.001). Semi-automated routing gave 95.9% accuracy, comparable to full manual review (p=0.610), with 68.9% workload reduction.
links.quote: This significant decrease in manual labor was accompanied by 95.9% in overall accuracy (Fig. 3 ), which was statistically comparable ( p = 0.610) to that achieved through fully IHC staining and manual evaluation by pathologists.

links.outcome: Accuracy at external centers with heterogeneous staining and scanning protocols
links.effect: At the 0.8 confidence cut-off, accuracy was 86.0% across 206 external patients from four centers. This compares with performance matching manual review at that cut-off in the internal data.
links.quote: In the external cohort comprising 206 patients from four external centers, the implementation of the semi-automated approach with a confidence cut-off of 0.8 yielded an accuracy of 86.0% (Fig. 3 ).

links.outcome: External-cohort accuracy after raising the confidence threshold
links.effect: Raising the cut-off from 0.8 to 0.9 improved accuracy from 86.0% to 95.1%, comparable to manual evaluation (p=0.293). Workload reduction fell to 39.3%.
links.quote: Under this scenario, although the workload reduction was only 39.3%, the accuracy significantly improved to 95.1%.

CTransPath-based semi-automated PitNET lineage classifier with confidence-threshold routing to IHC and manual review

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and workload reduction with confidence-based deferral to IHC and manual review
links.effect: In the prospective cohort, confidence-based deferral achieved 68.9% workload reduction and 95.9% overall accuracy; comparison with fully manual IHC-based evaluation: p = 0.610.
links.quote: In prospective validation, this approach achieved a 68.9% reduction in diagnostic workload while maintaining 95.9% overall accuracy.

links.outcome: Classification accuracy in external institutions with heterogeneous histopathological protocols
links.effect: Prospective-cohort accuracy was 95.9%; external-cohort accuracy was 86.0% at a confidence cut-off of 0.8, among 206 patients from four external centers.
links.quote: In the external cohort comprising 206 patients from four external centers, the implementation of the semi-automated approach with a confidence cut-off of 0.8 yielded an accuracy of 86.0% (Fig. 3 ).

links.outcome: External-cohort accuracy and workload reduction after confidence-threshold adjustment
links.effect: Raising the external-cohort confidence cut-off from 0.8 to 0.9 increased accuracy from 86.0% to 95.1%, with 39.3% workload reduction; comparison with manual evaluation: p = 0.293.
links.quote: Under this scenario, although the workload reduction was only 39.3%, the accuracy significantly improved to 95.1%.

links.effect: Setting a confidence threshold to route uncertain cases to manual review allowed the model's accuracy to match fully manual reviewing.
links.quote: Setting the confidence threshold above 0.8 allows the model’s accuracy to align closely with that achieved through fully manual reviewing ( p = 0.856).

links.effect: Using the fully automated model as a stand-alone diagnostic resulted in a 5.9% decrease in accuracy compared to standard-of-care manual review.
links.quote: However, it demonstrated a 5.9% decrease in accuracy and a 0.011 reduction in the AUC ( p < 0.001), compared to diagnoses based on IHC and manual review (Fig. 2 ).
